newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares hit new lows, more falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares hit new lows, more falls seen.

text.p: * Straits Times Industrials Index (STI) 1,974.37, (-15.43 pts) -- new year closing low
* Broad-based fall with more representative weighted DBS-50 index 497.30 (-10.66, or 2.10 percent)
* Car retailer Cycle & Carriage S$14.40 (-0.50), -- down on worries over motor division/property earnings
* New listing China drug firm Tianjin Zhongxin tops volume, debuts at US$1.05 vs US$0.68 IPO price
Singapore shares plunged to new lows on Friday on broad-based selling by foreign institutional investors and local dealers.
The unweighted Straits Times Industrials Index (STI) broke key psychological support of 1,980 points and hit a 45-month low at 1,968.66 before recovering slightly at the close.
The more representative, weighted DBS-50 index fell 10.66 points, or 2.1 percent, to 497.30. Total market volume was 188.6 million shares with 124 gainers to 228 losers.
Dealers said the market was likely to be quiet on Monday due to the public holiday in Hong Kong as the colony reverts to China.
But stocks were likely to tumble again once momentum picks up later next week with new lows seen highly likely by some technical analysts.
"I think we could see choppy trading early next week. But after that, falls are more likely than rises," said one dealer.
Of the 30 STI component stocks, car retailer Cycle & Carriage led the falls, down Singapore $0.50 at S$14.40 amid worries by some investors over the company's core motor division.
One dealer said Cycle & Carriage might be affected by keen competition from rival BMW and its property earnings could also be dampened by weaker prices.

Debutante Chinese drug firm Tianjin Zhongxin was well-received and dominated trade, with over 72.7 million shares changing hands. It closed at US$1.03 against its initial public offer price of US$0.68.
